question: Which festival is also known as the foundation day of Khalsa Panth?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Baisakhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Baisakhi** is celebrated as the foundation day of the **Khalsa Panth** by Sikhs.
 
• On **April 13, 1699**, Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the tenth Sikh Guru, established the Khalsa Panth.
 
• The creation of the Khalsa was a pivotal moment, marking the establishment of a community dedicated to righteousness and equality.
 
• Baisakhi also marks the beginning of the new harvest season and is celebrated with great fervor in Punjab and other parts of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khalsa Panth**

 
 
• The Khalsa Panth is a community of initiated Sikhs who adhere to the strict code of conduct and discipline defined by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
 
• Initiated Sikhs, known as Khalsa, are required to wear the five Ks: Kesh (uncut hair), Kara (a steel bracelet), Kanga (a wooden comb), Kachera (cotton undergarments), and Kirpan (a ceremonial sword).
 
• The Khalsa Panth was formed to uphold justice, righteousness, and to protect the oppressed.
 
 
 
• **Baisakhi Celebrations**
 
 
• Baisakhi is celebrated with processions known as Nagar Kirtans, which include singing hymns and displaying martial arts.
 
• Gurdwaras, the Sikh temples, are decorated, and special prayers are held to mark the occasion.
 
• Community meals, known as Langar, are served to all visitors, emphasizing the Sikh principles of equality and community service.
 
 
 
• **Harvest Festival**
 
 
• Baisakhi also signifies the harvest festival for the farming community in Punjab.
 
• It is a time of joy and celebration as farmers reap the fruits of their hard work.
 
• Traditional folk dances like Bhangra and Gidda are performed to celebrate the harvest.
